sentences.text: 1. The present acquittal Appeal has been filed by the appellant - R/CR.A/624/2006 JUDGMENT original complainant under Section 378(4) of Cr. P.C., against the Judgment and order dated 10.5.2002, rendered in P.F.A. Case No.67 of 2000 by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, (Municipal), Surat.
The said case was registered against the present respondents - original accused for the offence under sections 7(i) and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (for short "PFA Act").
The said Judgment of the trial Court has been challenged by the appellant on the ground that the Judgment and order passed by learned trial Court is against the law and evidence on record.

2. According to the prosecution case, on 26.2.1999, at about 12:00 p.m. at noon, the appellant - Food Inspector visited the respondent No.2 and at that time, accused No.2 was present and from him, the appellant purchased Micro Refine Kapasia oil in three plastic bottles by paying price of the same.
After following due procedure of sealing, packing etc. one sample was sent for analysis purpose.
Analyst report revealed the said sample of edible oil was adulterated and therefore, after obtaining sanction under Section 20 of the Act, the complaint was lodged against the accused persons.
Therefore, aforesaid Criminal Case was registered.
3. At the conclusion of trial and after appreciating the oral as well as documentary evidence, the learned trial Judge vide impugned Judgment, acquitted the respondents - accused.

4. Learned advocate Mr. Shah, appearing on behalf of the R/CR.A/624/2006 JUDGMENT appellant has contended that the Judgment and order of acquittal is contrary to law and evidence on record and is not proper.
He has contended that learned trial Judge has committed error in acquitting the accused on the ground that the public analyst himself had not tested the sample and he made only signature.
He also submitted that the accused were joined without any documents showing their involvement in the business.
He has contended that the trial Court has failed to appreciate the report of the Analyst.
He has also contended that the offences punishable under the Act are directly connected with the health of public at large.

5. Learned advocate Mr. Modi for the respondents - accused supported the impugned judgment and order of acquittal and he submitted that learned trial Judge has rightly appreciated the evidence produced on record and therefore, no interference is required to be called for.
He lastly submitted that present appeal may kindly be dismissed by confirming the impugned judgment and order of acquittal.

Learned advocate also cited the decisions of this Court passed in Criminal Appeal Nos.1686 of 2010, 500 of 1996, Criminal Misc. Application No.13589 of 2009 in Criminal Appeal No.2420 of 2009 and decision reported in 2009(1) Crimes 1 (Guj.).

sentences.text:
Heard learned APP Mrs. Hansa Punani for t**he R/CR.A/624/2006 JUDGMENT respondent No.4.
7.
I have gone through the papers produced in the case.
I have also gone through the evidence led before the trial Court as well as the Expert Opinion.
I have also gone through the Judgment of the trial Court.

In the case, the complainant has not produced original documents and report of analyst was not prepared by the public analyst himself and therefore, the accused cannot be held guilty for the offence as alleged.
Learned counsel for the appellant is unable to convince this court as to whether the prosecution has followed the mandatory provision of Rules.
In the facts of the case I am in complete agreement with the reasons assigned by the trial Court.
In view of this position, I am of the view that present case is covered up by the decisions cited by the learned advocate Mr. Modi for the respondents.
Hence, the appeal is required to be dismissed.

8. In the result, the Criminal Appeal is dismissed and order dated 10.5.2002 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Municipal Court, Surat, in P.F.A. Case No.67 of 2000 is hereby confirmed.
